score.notes: A confident three-gable composition — a tall central pediment flanked by two lower turret gables, each capped with a gold finial. The base→middle→crown reading is clear: a course-banded brick base with a recessed porch, a mid-register of framed windows, and a crown of stepped, gold-studded gables. Bay rhythm is deliberate and symmetric (paired vertical windows in each flanking tower mirror cleanly). Color is the strongest move: terracotta brick as dominant, eggplant-purple roofs as the supporting mass, gold as a disciplined accent on rakes/finials/window frames, with cool blue glass as a controlled secondary — genuinely colorful and harmonious, a Flemish/Hanseatic guildhall-temple identity. Detail is rich where it counts: gold-dotted stepped gable rakes, framed lancet windows, a tracery-filled blue rose/oculus over a recessed arched entrance with its own surround. Fidelity is high — it reads unmistakably as a grand civic temple with a clear, emphasized doorway and real frontal presence. What keeps every dimension at strong rather than exceptional: the large flat gold panel filling the central pediment is an inert field — its scale is slightly arbitrary and it carries no relief or ornament, the one easy improvement I can name. Break that gold plane with coursing, a relief emblem, or a recessed niche and the crown would resolve as well as the base. The brick fields are also a touch flat between openings. Resolved, intentional, and characterful end to end — a strong build, just short of iconic.
